paper_metadata.title: Mapping brain recovery after concussion: From acute injury to 1 year after medical clearance

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population, recruitment setting, and inclusion criteria. However, the sample size for the concussed group is small (n=24) compared to the control group (n=122), and there is no information on the total number of eligible athletes who declined participation, making it difficult to rule out selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Twenty-four concussed athletes were recruited consecutively from university-level sport teams at a single institution (including volleyball, hockey, soccer, football, rugby, basketball, lacrosse, and water polo)
items.reasoning: The authors specify the population as university-level athletes across multiple sports at a single institution.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: recruited consecutively from university-level sport teams... through the academic sport medicine clinic after concussion diagnosis.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment from a specialized clinic is a standard method to reduce selection bias.

items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Diagnosis was determined by a staff physician after a sustained direct or indirect contact to the head with the presence of signs or symptoms as per the Concussion in Sport Group guidelines with standard neurologic assessment conducted
items.reasoning: The study uses established international guidelines (CISG) for diagnosis and specifies the 'zero time' as the point of injury/diagnosis.

items.label: Baseline characteristics

items.evidence_snippet: Participant demographics are listed in table 1, including age, sex, and concussion history, along with time to RTP for concussed athletes.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive breakdown of age, sex, prior history, and baseline SCAT3 scores.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study implies a 100% completion rate for the longitudinal scans of the 24 concussed athletes. While the sample is small, the lack of dropouts in the primary cohort minimizes attrition bias.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: 24 athletes with concussion were scanned longitudinally within 1 week after injury, at RTP, and 1 year after RTP.
items.reasoning: The text indicates all 24 recruited athletes completed the three-stage longitudinal protocol.

items.evidence_snippet: None of the concussed athletes had acquired a new concussion between the SYM and 1-year post-RTP scanning time points
items.reasoning: Since no dropouts are reported for the concussed group, this item is satisfied by the implication of full follow-up.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (acute symptom severity and time to RTP) are measured using standardized clinical tools (SCAT3) and a supervised medical protocol. The measurement is consistent across the cohort.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: specifically SCAT3 total symptom severity score at acute injury and days to RTP, defined as the number of days from the concussion event to symptom resolution, following a graded exertional protocol.
items.reasoning: The PFs are clearly defined as the SCAT3 severity score and the duration of the RTP protocol.

items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes in the study completed baseline assessments with the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3)
items.reasoning: SCAT3 is a validated, standard-of-care tool in sports medicine.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: a composite measure was produced by renormalizing via inverse empirical distribution function, mean centering, and then averaging the 2 variables.
items.reasoning: The authors used continuous composite scores rather than arbitrary binary cut-offs.

items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes in the study completed baseline assessments... Athletes diagnosed with a concussion also completed SCAT3 assessments at acute injury and time of RTP
items.reasoning: The protocol was standardized for all concussed participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcomes are objective MRI measures (Gconn, CBF, FA, MD) obtained using standardized 3T protocols and validated software pipelines. The use of objective imaging significantly reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Each imaging session assessed global functional connectivity (Gconn) and cerebral blood flow (CBF), along with white matter fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD).
items.reasoning: The outcomes are clearly defined as specific quantitative MRI parameters.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Athletes were imaged using a 3T MRI system (Magnetom Skyra, Siemens Healthineers USA, Malvern, PA) with a standard multichannel head coil.
items.reasoning: 3T MRI is the gold standard for research; the paper details extensive preprocessing steps (AFNI, FSL) to ensure data quality.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The magnetization prepared rapid acquisition gradient edge imaging, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery imaging, and susceptibility-weighted imaging scans were inspected by an MRI technologist during imaging and later reviewed by a neuroradiologist
items.reasoning: All participants underwent the same imaging protocol on the same scanner.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study uses a sophisticated matching process for the control group (matching on sex, age, and prior concussion), the small sample size limits the ability to adjust for multiple confounders simultaneously in a multivariable model. The authors acknowledge that factors like sport type and physical fitness were not fully controlled.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Participant demographics are listed in table 1, including age, sex, and concussion history
items.reasoning: Key demographics are measured, but other potential confounders like 'detraining' or 'subconcussive impacts' during the 1-year follow-up were not measured.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: control athletes were selected who matched the concussed athlete on sex and prior concussion; within this pool, controls who had ≤2 years of age difference from the concussed athlete were selected
items.reasoning: The matching criteria for confounders are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes in the study completed baseline assessments with the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool 3 (SCAT3) before the beginning of their respective athletic seasons.
items.reasoning: Concussion history and baseline status were recorded prospectively at the start of the season.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes in the study completed baseline assessments... before the beginning of their respective athletic seasons.
items.reasoning: Baseline data collection was uniform for both groups.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: the MRI parameter values xs were first converted into difference scores relative to a subgroup of matched controls
items.reasoning: The study used a matched-control design to account for age, sex, and history.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: The present study measured concussion effects within a demographically mixed cohort... but future large cohort studies should directly evaluate the influence of demographic factors
items.reasoning: While matching was used, the small sample size (n=24) prevented complex multivariable adjustment for all potential interactions.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, using nonparametric bootstrapping and cluster-size thresholding to handle the multiple comparisons inherent in voxel-wise neuroimaging. The reporting is transparent regarding both significant and non-significant findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: the effects of concussion were evaluated with voxel-wise nonparametric analyses... bootstrapped empirical distributions were obtained by resampling on participants with replacement (1,000 iterations).
items.reasoning: The analytical pipeline is described in high detail, including software and specific statistical parameters.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: A secondary analysis determined whether the neuroimaging measures of concussed athletes were influenced by clinical factors, specifically SCAT3 total symptom severity score at acute injury and days to RTP
items.reasoning: The choice of covariates (symptoms and RTP time) is clinically grounded in concussion recovery models.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Significant brain regions were identified where the 99.5% confidence interval (CI) did not overlap zero... cluster-size thresholding was performed at an adjusted p = 0.05
items.reasoning: The use of bootstrapping and cluster-correction is appropriate for longitudinal neuroimaging data.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Both Gconn and FA displayed no significant effects at 1 year after RTP, whereas CBF and MD exhibited persistent long-term effects.
items.reasoning: The authors report both the resolution of some markers and the persistence of others, matching their stated hypothesis testing.
